# smelt

> smelt is an open-source coding agent for the terminal. It has a Rust core and is configured and extended in Lua, like Neovim. It supports ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Kimi Code and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and runs on Linux, macOS and Windows. It is in beta until 1.0, so interfaces may change between releases.

Install: `curl -fsSL https://smeltagent.dev/install.sh | sh`

Source: https://github.com/leonardcser/smelt

## Guide

- [Getting started](https://smeltagent.dev/guide/getting-started/): install, log in with `smelt auth`, first prompt
- [Common workflows](https://smeltagent.dev/guide/workflows/): attach files, review changes, run hands-off, resume sessions
- [Headless and CI](https://smeltagent.dev/guide/headless/): run without the TUI in scripts and pipelines
- [Benchmarks](https://smeltagent.dev/guide/benchmarks/): Terminal-Bench 2.1 resource use against five other agents
- [Troubleshooting](https://smeltagent.dev/guide/troubleshooting/): common problems and fixes

## Customize

- [Configure smelt with Lua](https://smeltagent.dev/customize/): init.lua, project config, reloading, load order
- [Providers and models](https://smeltagent.dev/customize/providers/): register providers, choose models and reasoning
- [Settings](https://smeltagent.dev/customize/settings/): every setting in init.lua
- [Themes and keymaps](https://smeltagent.dev/customize/appearance/): bundled themes, file icons, keymaps
- [Custom commands](https://smeltagent.dev/customize/commands/): Markdown and Lua slash commands
- [Skills, MCP servers and AGENTS.md](https://smeltagent.dev/customize/agent/): instructions, skills, MCP
